subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should OpenClaw change externally registered recurring cron jobs to a safer activation/provenance and spend-guard model, and what compatibility path should existing jobs get?
rationale: The evidence supports the safety gap, but changing cron activation defaults, model inheritance, quota thresholds, and doctor/update behavior can intentionally stop existing background automation or require migrations, so maintainer security/product intent is required before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor core cron safety design
options.body: Define provenance, activation confirmation, safe model defaults, and budget/circuit-breaker behavior in core, with doctor/upgrade handling for existing jobs.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Keep or create focused items for activation consent, provenance, reason-aware retries, and cost budgets, then close this broad issue only after every subproblem is explicitly tracked.

options.title: Keep operator-trust defaults
options.body: Decide that current operator-admin cron semantics are intentional, document the cost/security tradeoff, and route only optional guardrails to follow-up proposals.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core cron safety design
recommendation.body: Define provenance, activation confirmation, safe model defaults, and budget/circuit-breaker behavior in core, with doctor/upgrade handling for existing jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current cron behavior blames to steipete-authored/merged history, and the decision crosses core security/default policy rather than a local test-only repair.
